summary: The iterative implementation passes the existing write-boundary suite, but still overflows the stack on large literals containing long runs of leading or internal spaces. It also changes unmatched single-quote fragments that the previous implementation preserved.

findings.claim: Spreading trailingSpaces into push passes one function argument per space, so a sufficiently long run of spaces followed by a non-space still throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The same defect exists at line 55 before an escaped quote. A roughly 15-million-character literal with 200,000 internal spaces reproduces the exact failure this task requires eliminating; flush by iteration or append string slices instead of spreading an unbounded array.

The scanner always appends a closing quote, even when it reached EOF without finding one, and discards any buffered spaces. Thus an unmatched quote changes input outside any recognized quote pair: prefix followed by an unterminated literal is silently rewritten rather than preserved as before. Only commit trimming after finding a closing quote; preserve an unmatched suffix verbatim.
